observation.visible_scene: A close-up nighttime view of a wood fire: several logs and thin sticks are piled at an angle, with a bright glowing ember bed along the bottom and a dark metal grate-like structure on the right. Tall yellow-white flames rise from the center of the pile. The log arrangement, ember bed, and right-side structure stay in fixed positions throughout, indicating the camera is essentially static.
visible_changes: The flames continuously deform, flicker, and change shape from frame to frame, with no single stable form.

The main flame body shifts laterally: tongues of flame extend toward the left in some frames (e.g., around t=0.24-0.64s and t=1.44-2.00s) and contract back toward a more vertical central plume in others (e.g., t=0.80-1.28s and t=2.08-2.80s).
A separate small flame and faint bluish glow appear intermittently on the right side near the thick log, more visible in the later frames (t≈2.64-3.20s).
Thin grayish smoke wisps drift upward above the flames, becoming more noticeable in the middle-to-late portion of the clip.
The overall brightness of the fire pulses but the ember bed at the bottom remains persistently lit.
outside_clip_unknowns: The fire is already burning at the first frame and still burning at the last; its ignition and eventual outcome lie outside the excerpt.
The fuel source and any cause of the wind/flicker are not shown.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is judged minimal/none because background logs and the right grate hold constant positions, but slight handheld jitter cannot be fully excluded.
Whether any individual stick physically moves is unclear; apparent motion is dominated by flame deformation rather than object translation.
observation.persistent_properties: Fixed log/stick pile, continuously glowing ember bed, dark surrounding background, and the right-side metal structure remain unchanged across the segment.
